pre-commit.description: Renovate's pre-commit manager is opt-in. Without this the hook revisions in .pre-commit-config.yaml are the one dependency file nobody is watching.

packageRules.description: Minor, patch and digest updates are not merged automatically: every update needs review

A Renovate major can raise engines.node past the node-version that .github/workflows/renovate.yml sets up, leaving every hourly run on a Node that Renovate does not support. This note reaches the reviewer of the bump.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Before merging, check this version's `engines.node` (`npm view renovate@<version> engines`) against `node-version` in `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`. If it no longer accepts that Node major, raise `node-version` in the same pull request, and in shakenfist/development's `templates/renovate/renovate.yml`, which every repository copies verbatim.

packageRules.description: Renovate's github-actions manager proposes Node majors for setup-node, and .github/workflows/renovate.yml must stay on a Node that the pinned Renovate's engines.node accepts, or every hourly run fails with "Unsupported node environment detected". That Node is raised by hand, in the pull request for the Renovate major that needs it (see the rule above), never on its own. Node in other workflows is unaffected.

shellcheck-py tags a fourth packaging component -- v0.11.0.1 is shellcheck 0.11.0, packaging revision 1 -- which is not semver, so without this the github-tags lookup behind the pre-commit hook fails with "Can't find version matching" on the dependency dashboard and no update is ever proposed. The fourth group is named build rather than revision: Renovate's regex versioning only compares revision when a build group matched too, so naming it revision would make v0.11.0.2 compare equal to v0.11.0.1 and hide packaging-only releases. The anchor to exactly four numeric components ignores re-tags such as v0.11.0.1-1. Harmless in a repository that does not use the hook. See templates/renovate/README.md in shakenfist/development.

Group RustCrypto digest-ecosystem crates so they upgrade in lockstep. The `digest` trait crate is shared by sha*, hmac, rsa, signature, etc., and a major bump of one (e.g. sha1 0.10 -> 0.11 moves to digest 0.11) breaks compilation against any sibling still on the old `digest` major. Keeping them in one PR forces them to land together.

Group webrtc with its sans-io core rtc so they upgrade in lockstep. webrtc pins rtc to an exact patch and exposes rtc types (Packet, RtpCodecKind, RTCRtpCodecParameters) in its public API, so bumping either alone puts two rtc versions in the graph and shakenfist-spice-webrtc fails to compile (see #393 / #394).

Group openh264 with openh264-sys2 so they upgrade in lockstep. shakenfist-spice-compression pins both exactly: its H.264 encoder sets options through openh264-sys2's raw types that openh264 does not re-export, so the pair must be the one openh264 was released with, and bumping either alone either fails to resolve or puts two openh264-sys2 builds in the graph.

Hold sha1 < 0.11 until rsa 0.10 stable releases. sha1 0.11 moves to digest 0.11, but our transitive rsa 0.9 still requires digest 0.10, so Sha1 no longer satisfies rsa::Oaep::new's DynDigest bound. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
Hold rand < 0.9 until rsa 0.10 stable releases. rand 0.9 restructured CryptoRngCore, which rsa 0.9 calls through. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
Hold rand_core < 0.10 to stay aligned with the rand 0.8 / rsa 0.9 pin above. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
